chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad narrated to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abdullah ibn Khalid al-Kinani, who said:

Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) faced me while I had a fish hanging in my hand. He said, 'Throw it away. I dislike for the noble man to carry cheap things himself.' Then he said, 'O Shia, your enemies are many. O people of Shia, the creation has been hostile to you, so adorn yourselves for them as much as you are able.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic teaching on maintaining dignity and discretion in front of enemies?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) emphasizes the importance of dignity and discretion for the Shia. It advises against carrying cheap items personally to avoid appearing humble or lowly, and encourages maintaining a good appearance before enemies who are numerous and hostile.
